verdict.rationale: Pinecone's own security docs say it manages API key permissions in the console and uses role-based access controls (RBAC) on resources, alongside service accounts and SSO. That covers the API-key and role parts of the story. Nothing in the pack shows permissions scoped per index or namespace, and the RBAC evidence is thin. Missing for 10: documented per-index/per-namespace (per-collection) permission scoping, detail on role definitions and which operations each role can perform, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can enforce granular access control (API keys, roles, per-collection permissions) on database operations

citations.quote: You can manage API key permissions in the Pinecone console... Pinecone uses role-based access controls (RBAC) to manage access to resources.
Overview of Pinecone security features for production: API keys, SSO, service accounts, audit logs, CMEK encryption, backups, and Private Endpoints.
SSO allows organizations to manage their teams’ access to Pinecone through their identity management solution.
